$comment: One case per limit in docs/DESIGN.md §10. Every case must produce a
LIMIT_EXCEEDED diagnostic, never a crash and never a hang.
Cases whose input is small enough to read are committed as files. Cases
whose input is a multi-hundred-kilobyte or multi-megabyte bomb are declared
here and generated by test/dos.test.ts from these parameters — an 80 MB
base64 data URI does not belong in a git history that is about to be public.
A generated case is no less a fixture: the parameters are the fixture.
The four `measured: true` cases were run against the pinned dependency
versions on 2026-08-05. They are not hypotheses.

cases.observed: parse5 is O(depth²), not O(bytes): 25 KB → 67 ms, 100 KB → 982 ms, 200 KB → 3.9 s.
cases.why: The 8 MB byte cap and the 100 k node cap both PASS this input — 440 KB and 40 001 nodes. Only a pre-parse depth gate catches it, because the cost and the crash both happen during the parse.

cases.observed: acorn parses it in 6 ms; acorn-walk throws RangeError immediately.
cases.why: No byte or node limit sees this. The recursion is in the walker, so containment is the only answer.
Panelint's own traversals are iterative with an explicit stack. domutils' is not, and every rule that reads text goes through it.

cases.limit: maxCssRules is not the relevant one
cases.observed: css-select throws RangeError while COMPILING, before any node is tested.
cases.why: One rule, one selector. The 20 k CSS-rule cap and the node count both pass it.
PANE-HIDDEN-010 must not decode an 80 MB data URI. The decoded size is arithmetic on the encoded length, so the cap is checked BEFORE any Buffer.from call.
resources/read is uncapped by the SDK. One resource can be any size the server chooses.
A server can list any number of ui:// resources. The per-resource budget does not bound the total.
